how: Each publisher page, GitHub repo (through the gh API) and public Figma Community page was opened without signing in and the licence read from it; Figma started showing a human-verification check partway through, so later Figma files are recorded from the search results only and marked unchecked.
second_check: 2026-11-10, a second pass after the search: (1) the 27 GitHub-hosted entries were re-checked against GitHub's own licence field; all 27 exist and none is archived. (2) The 10 Penpot entries were changed to licence-not-confirmed, because their CC-BY-4.0 comes from a README line, not a licence file or the item's own page. (3) 26 Figma Community file pages the search could not open were opened and their licence line read (25 say CC BY 4.0, 1 is Apple's design-resources licence). Figma then showed a human-verification check, so the remaining Figma entries stay unconfirmed. Nobody signed in or completed that check.

published: Only entries with an open licence read from the source are in this file, each with the credit to give. Kits under their publisher's own terms (Apple's design resources, for one) and files whose licence could not be read are kept out of the published catalog.
